title: Open detail D1b · The box's two buttons on a small phone
subtitle: From item 8; for Main's shared confirm box. Item 8's words (the safe button says “Keep …”, the other repeats the pressed words) make the labels longer. On a 320 px phone, Color Belt's “Keep student” and “Delete permanently” already squeeze onto two lines each; longer pairs will too. Rule §2.1 allows a full-width button on a phone only for a form's single submit button, so stacking needs a small exception written into §2.1. Which button goes first is the next question (D1c); here they keep today's order. (Preview screenshots as a touch screen · fake data)

row.caption: 1. 320 px wide (small phones): “Keep student” and “Delete permanently” squeeze onto two lines each.
2. 390 px wide: they fit side by side.

columns.label: Option B (recommended) and option C, drawn

row.caption: 3. Option B at 320 px: when they don't fit, the two buttons stack, each the full width of the box, in the row's order. At 390 px they stay side by side (picture 2).
4. Option C: stacked on every phone, even when they would fit (390 px here).

columns.note: Pictures 3–4 are drawn over the real box; nothing in the app was changed.

footer:
Your choice — one question: what happens when a box's two buttons don't fit on one line?
A · Keep as today. + no work. − on small phones the words break onto two lines each, and item 8's longer “Keep …” pairs make it worse.
B · Recommended: stack them only when they don't fit (picture 3). + every label on one line and big targets on the smallest phones; everywhere else the box looks as today. − the box looks a little different on a 320 px phone; §2.1 gets a small exception.
C · Stack them on every phone (picture 4). + one look on every phone; the biggest targets. − taller boxes on phones where the buttons fit side by side; a bigger §2.1 exception.
